# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to transmit the manual’s three mappings to Deaf visually. I’ll use a simple numeric code: 👆 = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3, and 🙏 separates entries. The entries are given in the manual’s row order: blue→green, green→yellow, red→red. Deaf can match the visible light and relay the required wire color to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "🙏", "✌", "✌", "🙏", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual and tell me its exact procedure. Also obtain from Deaf the exact display, light, and wire markings or colours, identifying wires 1, 2, and 3. Relay all facts precisely; do not guess.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0. The light is red. Wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Please use the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.

The red light selects the manual’s red row, which requires cutting the red wire. Deaf reports that wire 1 is red, so Blind must cut wire 1. I will signal Deaf the wire number; Deaf can speak the full instruction to Blind, including the manual procedure and all observed markings.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no facts. Please immediately state the manual's exact rule and relay Deaf's exact observations for DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1, 2, and 3, including any colours, symbols, or numbers.
Deaf says to Mute: Your gesture has no agreed meaning. Please relay the manual's exact required action to Blind using speech.

The manual says: for a red light, cut a red wire. Deaf observed a red light and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, so the required action is to cut wire 1. Since I cannot speak, I am using the unambiguous one-finger sign for wire number 1; Deaf already has the observations and can state the full rule and instruction to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf cannot hear me, so watch Deaf's next gestures and translate them into spoken words for me. Ask Deaf to report the display, light, and each wire's colour and marking, then relay the complete report.
Deaf says to Mute: State unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Please speak the manual's exact action to Blind; do not rely on gestures.

The exact manual action is to cut the red wire. Deaf’s unchanged report identifies wire 1 as red, so Blind must cut wire 1. I cannot speak to Blind; I will again visibly indicate wire 1 to Deaf, who can state the complete action aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No facts have reached me. Establish a fixed gesture code with Deaf: use distinct gestures for wires 1, 2, and 3, and agree how Deaf will signal each visible colour or marking. Then ask Deaf for DISPLAY, LIGHT, and all three wires. Read the manual exactly and speak the complete decoded report to me next turn.
Deaf says to Mute: Use this code for the manual answer: first gesture is the wire, ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Second gesture is the action, 👌 means cut and ✋ means do not cut. Send both gestures in order.

The manual maps the red light to cutting a red wire. Deaf’s report says wire 1 is red, so the encoded answer is wire 1 followed by “cut.” I will send the agreed two-gesture code to Deaf, who can speak the decoded instruction to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your spoken message reaches me directly. Do not wait for another turn or merely ask Deaf: speak the manual's exact cut rule and Deaf's complete observations of DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1, 2, and 3 now. If Deaf has not answered, say that explicitly.

I cannot speak directly to Blind. Deaf has already provided the complete observations: display 0; red light; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. The manual requires cutting a red wire, therefore wire 1. I will resend the established wire-1/cut code to Deaf so Deaf can speak the full report and instruction to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌"])
```
